title: Consecutive loan streaks
statementMd:
For member 1, group their loan dates into streaks where consecutive loans are at most 30 days apart, and show each streak's start, end and size. Order by start.

Expected columns: `streak_start`, `streak_end`, `loans`.

Tables: `authors`, `books`, `members`, `loans`.

**Row order matters** for this problem.
hints: `LAG` to flag gaps over 30 days, running sum of the flags to number the streaks.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH d AS (SELECT loan_date, CASE WHEN julianday(loan_date) - julianday(LAG(loan_date) OVER (ORDER BY loan_date, id)) > 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_streak FROM loans WHERE member_id = 1), g AS (SELECT loan_date, SUM(new_streak) OVER (ORDER BY loan_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS grp FROM d) SELECT MIN(loan_date) AS streak_start, MAX(loan_date) AS streak_end, COUNT(*) AS loans FROM g GROUP BY grp ORDER BY streak_start;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
